_readme: This file is the whole site. Edit here, not in the pages.

PRODUCT (default item type): fill 'name' to make it appear. Fields: slot (what goes here), brand, name, image, desc, why (Why I rate it), price, discount, code, link (affiliate URL). Empty fields are not shown. No 'name' = hidden on the live site. No 'link' = no SHOP button.

INFO item (type 'info'): an educational breakdown. Fields: name, status (established | cosmetic | prescription | experimental), body, story, provider (true = shows the licensed-provider line), link. A SHOP button only ever shows for established or cosmetic items. No 'body' = hidden on the live site.
MY EXPERIENCE: every info item has a 'story' field. Write Chad's real experience there in his own words. Empty = not shown on the live site. Never invent one.
PROVIDER item (type 'provider'): a line pointing to a licensed medical provider or test provider. Fields: label, link. No 'link' = hidden on the live site.
Hidden items still show as grey DRAFT slots when you open the site on this computer, or anywhere with ?draft=1 on the address.
config.trackEndpoint: optional URL that receives every affiliate click as JSON. Clicks are also sent to Google Analytics or Plausible if either is installed on the page.

COPY: 'body' and 'story' can be one string or a list of paragraphs. 'lead' is a short line under the name. A stack can have 'outro': {title, lines[], fine} shown under the cards. A section 'title' can be empty.

PHOTOS: a stack can have 'photos': a list of {before, after, caption, beforeLabel, afterLabel}. A pair only shows if both image files exist. For hair, drop files into images/hair/ named before-1.jpg, after-1.jpg, before-2.jpg, after-2.jpg.
PHOTO PINS: each photo pair can have 'beforePin' and 'afterPin': {x, y, text}. x and y are percentages across and down the photo where the marker points. Change 'text' to relabel it.
CARD PHOTO: an info item can have 'photo': {before, after, beforeLabel, afterLabel, beforePin, afterPin}. It shows inside that card, above the text.

stacks.name: The Hair Stack
stacks.tagline: Thicker, fuller hair. Keep what you've got.
stacks.desc: The Norwood Reaper comes for everyone. Don't wait until your hairline is halfway across your scalp to start caring. Discover my complete hair optimization stack, covering hair preservation, thickness, volume and elite styling.
stacks.headline: Keep it. Thicken it.
stacks.sub: Hold your hairline. Grow it back. Make it look good.
intro: Way too many guys wait until they notice hair loss to start a hair loss protocol. That's the biggest mistake you can make.
You can lose around half the hair in a spot before it's even visible. By the time you notice, the damage is already done.
Most men deal with this at some point. Some just slower than others.
Don't wait until it's too late to start a protocol.

items.name: Finasteride
items.body: Blocks DHT, the hormone behind male pattern hair loss. Used to stop the hairline going back. Oral or topical.

items.name: Dutasteride
items.body: A stronger DHT blocker. The step up when finasteride isn't enough.

items.name: Minoxidil 5%
items.body: Topical foam or liquid, used to regrow and thicken hair.

items.name: Ketoconazole shampoo
items.body: Anti-dandruff shampoo, used alongside the rest for scalp health and hair.

items.name: Derma stamp (microneedling)
items.body: Used with minoxidil to push regrowth further.

items.name: GHK-Cu copper peptide serum
items.body: Copper peptide serum for the scalp, used for hair thickness.

items.name: GHK-Cu, injectable
items.body: Copper peptide, used for hair and skin quality.

sections.title: The Styling Arsenal
sections.note: Having hair is one thing. Knowing what to do with it is another.

stacks.name: The Skinmaxx Stack
stacks.tagline: Clear skin. Fewer breakouts. Protect your halo.
stacks.desc: The last thing you want is an aesthetic physique, elite hair and fucked-up skin. From androgen-related breakouts to premature aging, your skin can make or break your halo. Discover my complete skinmaxxing stack, covering clear skin, anti-aging, skin quality, peptides and my go-to products.
stacks.headline: Don't let bad skin kill your work.
stacks.sub: Clear skin. Elite complexion. Age like a Chad.
intro: We put all this work into the gym and dieting. If you don't have clear skin and a nice complexion, it will hold you back.
The goal for me is clear, healthy-looking skin, an even complexion and a natural glow without having a ridiculous 15-step skincare routine.

items.name: GHK-Cu
body: GHK-Cu is a copper peptide that interests me because of its potential role in skin repair, collagen production and overall skin quality. Evidence for injectable use remains limited.

items.name: Melanotan II
body: I've always preferred how I look with a tan.
Melanotan II is something I've experimented with in the past. It's an unapproved tanning compound that carries significant health risks, so my experience isn't a recommendation to use it.

items.name: KPV
story: I've tried a ton of things for my acne over the years. Cleansers, creams, treatments, all of it.
Nothing cleared my skin up as much as KPV, and nothing else has kept it away like this.
It's still an experimental peptide, so take this as my experience, not a promise.

sections.title: Anti-Aging
sections.note: The goal isn't just to look good now. It's to look good ten years from now.

items.name: Adapalene 0.1%
body: Adapalene is one of the more established options for managing acne and improving skin texture over time. Nothing flashy, just a legitimate skincare ingredient that doesn't need some ridiculous marketing gimmick.

sections.title: Instant Aesthetic Upgrades
sections.note: Sometimes you've got a date in two hours and your skin didn't get the fucking memo.

items.name: Tinted Moisturizer
body: One of the most underrated products for men.
The goal isn't to look like you're wearing makeup. It's to even out your complexion, subtly cover imperfections and make your skin look naturally better.

outro.title: Max out your complexion.
lines: Your face is the first thing people see. Give it the same attention you give your physique.

stacks.name: The Lean & Mean Stack
stacks.tagline: Lean, chiseled, movie star physique. Not bloated.
stacks.desc: Being 250 pounds doesn't automatically make you aesthetic. The objective isn't to become a refrigerator with arms. It's to build a lean, muscular physique with proportions that actually look good. Discover my personal stack for leanmaxxing, physique optimization, performance and recovery.
stacks.headline: Build an aesthetic physique. Not a refrigerator.
intro: The goal for me is the movie-star physique. Broad shoulders, a narrow waist, visible abs and a sharp fucking jawline.
I want to look good 365 days a year without making my entire existence revolve around dieting.

items.name: Retatrutide
body: One of the biggest challenges for me when staying lean has always been the constant food noise. Thinking about your next meal 24/7 gets exhausting pretty fucking quickly.
Retatrutide is something I've personally experimented with throughout my transformation while working toward a leaner physique.

items.name: Tirzepatide
body: I'm not interested in spending half the year bulking and the other half suffering through an aggressive cut.
I've explored tirzepatide as part of my approach to appetite management.

items.name: Tesamorelin
body: Tesamorelin is a little different from the other compounds in this stack. Rather than suppressing appetite, it stimulates your body's natural growth hormone production.
I've experimented with it alongside retatrutide or tirzepatide because they work through different pathways. My goal has always been to get lean while maintaining as much muscle as possible.

outro.title: Stay lean. Stay muscular. Enjoy your life.
lines: Looking good shouldn't be something you only do for six weeks of the year.

stacks.name: The Primal Stack
stacks.desc: Looking like a Chad is only half the equation. What's the point of looking elite if you've got the energy and sex drive of a retired accountant? Discover my personal male vitality stack, covering libido, energy, performance, recovery, compounds and peptides.
stacks.headline: Reclaim your primal edge.
intro: Every guy wants to max out his looks, but very few talk about maxing out their confidence in the bedroom.
Personally, I want to give the woman I'm with an experience she'll remember. I don't want to spend half the night in my own head worrying about how I'm going to perform.

items.name: Tadalafil
story: For me, the biggest difference has been confidence. I've had nights where I haven't performed the way I wanted to, and that shit is frustrating.
Being able to get out of my own head, enjoy the moment and focus on the woman I'm with makes a massive difference to my experience.

items.name: PT-141
items.lead: The desire side of the equation.
body: There's a difference between being physically ready and genuinely wanting to rip each other's clothes off.
That's what makes the subject of libido so interesting to me. It's an entirely different conversation from erection quality, and something most guys rarely discuss openly.

outro.title: The bottom line
lines: Looking your best is one thing. Being confident when it actually matters is another.
outro.fine: Personal experiences are not guaranteed results. Prescription treatments require medical guidance.
